newsitem.title: DENMARK: Clinton says he is not upset by Chretien comments.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says he is not upset by Chretien comments.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday brushed aside critical comments made about him by Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, saying it would not affect their relationship.
"He's a superior human being," Clinton said during a chat with reporters as he travelled to Denmark from Romania. "He's a very fine, a very great leader."
During the NATO summit in Madrid earlier this week, Chretien made some stinging comments about Clinton as he and others waited for the U.S. president to show up for a photo call.
In unguarded remarks to Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, Chretien was overheard criticising Clinton for approving only three new NATO members and not five, as Canada and others had hoped.
"It's not for reasons of security," Chretien was reported to have said. "It's all done for short-term political reasons to win elections."
Chretien's comments, made in French, were picked up by a microphone left on inadvertently near the two prime ministers, who were unaware their conversation was being recorded.
"You know, this is just not going to bother me," Clinton said, joking that he would "get even" on the golf course. The two leaders have played golf together in Washington.

A senior U.S. official said White House National Security Adviser Samuel Berger had been upset by the remarks and was even angrier when a Canadian official tried to describe the comments as something "said affectionately".
